thread:
maria: Quick PSA — we're putting a partial release freeze on model-serving changes starting 15:00 UTC today due to a canary latency spike observed in the quant-plugin rollout. :warning:

samir: Thx. Which lanes are blocked? only `main` or canary branches too?

maria: Blocks: any PR that modifies runtime kernels, batching, or quantization flags. Canaries deploying the plugin will be paused automatically. Non-runtime work (docs, perf tests) ok to merge.

dev-bot: [alert] Canary 03 reported p50 latency +45% and a 3% error increase at 14:12 UTC. Trace: https://internal.redwood.co/trace/cc3f

olivia: Are Dedicated customers impacted?

maria: Dedicated clusters are not affected by the hosted canary pipeline, but don't merge changes that would diverge runtime behavior without a coordinated rollout. If you need an exception for a security patch, tag @maria and @olivia and include the `security-exempt` label.

kai: Quick question on rollback: if we see the same spike after landing a fix, do we force-rollback or gate with canary sweep?

maria: Prefer canary sweep + patch when possible. If host production latency crosses the SLA threshold we execute the immediate rollback playbook. Runbook: https://internal.redwood.co/runbooks/canary-latency

samir: Copy. For visibility, I'm going to open a short-lived dashboard with filtered quant-plugin metrics and add it to the release channel.

ana (typo correction) <-- note: IUser typed wrong

ana is typo — should be ana.

ana: (oops) :sweat_smile:

ana: ack, I'll update the docs and the onboarding checklist to mention the temporary freeze and the exception path.

maria: Thanks. Plan: freeze in effect until 09:00 UTC tomorrow unless we confirm the plugin health across canaries. We'll post updates in this thread. Please escalate regressions to #incidents and ping @olivia if you see production impact. :white_check_mark:
